examples.ko: 영어를 잘하는 친구가 저를 위해 통역해요.
examples.en: A friend who speaks English well interprets for me.
I interpreted English into Korean at the meeting.

examples.ko: 말을 바로 통역하는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Interpreting speech on the spot isn't easy.

examples.ko: 한국어를 아주 잘하면 통역할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you speak Korean very well, you can interpret.
Don't worry, I'll interpret for you.
I couldn't eat lunch because I was interpreting.

explain: '통역'은 말을 소리로 바로 옮기는 일이고, 글을 옮기는 일은 '번역'이에요. 그래서 회의에서는 '통역', 책이나 문서는 '번역'이라고 해요. 직업 이름은 '통역사'이고, '통역해 주다'를 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 친구가 저 대신 한국어로 통역해 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend interpreted into Korean for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙여 다른 사람을 도와서 통역할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 주다 means interpreting as a help to someone.

phrases.en: My uncle works as an interpreter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통역을 직업으로 하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person whose job is interpreting.

phrases.en: At the meeting, I interpreted Korean into English.
phrases.nuance_ko: '(으)로'를 붙여 어떤 언어로 옮기는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses (으)로 to say which language the speech is interpreted into.

explain_en: '통역' is carrying spoken words across languages on the spot, while moving written text is '번역'. So you use '통역' at meetings and '번역' for books and documents. The job is '통역사', and '통역해 주다' (interpret for someone) is common.

t90.ax: Don't worry, I'll interpret for you.

examples.en: The teacher's board writing is neat, so it is easy to take notes.

examples.ko: 오늘 수업은 판서가 많아서 손이 아팠어요.
examples.en: There was a lot of board writing in today's class, so my hand hurt.
I took a photo of what was written on the board.
The professor explains only by speaking, without writing on the board.

examples.ko: 요즘은 판서 대신 화면으로 수업하는 학교도 많아요.
examples.en: These days many schools teach with screens instead of the board.
I can't see the board writing well from the back seats.

explain: 선생님이 칠판이나 화이트보드에 쓰는 글씨를 말해요. 학생이 공책에 적는 '필기'와 짝으로 기억하면 좋고, '판서하다'로도 써요.

phrases.en: The teacher writes the important points on the board.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '판서'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사로, 칠판에 쓰는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form: the act of writing on the board.

phrases.example: 시험 전에 판서 내용을 다시 읽어 봤어요.
phrases.en: I reread what was written on the board before the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칠판에 적힌 수업 내용을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to lesson content that was written on the board.

phrases.en: I copied what was on the board into my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생이 필기하는 모습과 이어서 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connects the teacher's writing to the student's note-taking.

explain_en: It refers to what a teacher writes on a chalkboard or whiteboard. It is easy to remember as a pair with '필기', which is what students write in their notebooks, and it can also be used as '판서하다'.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 단속반이 우리 동네에 왔어요.
examples.en: An enforcement team came to our neighborhood this morning.
I moved my car before the enforcement team came out.

examples.ko: 저는 음식점 위생을 점검하는 단속반에서 일해요.
examples.en: I work on a team that inspects restaurant hygiene.
The enforcement team walks the streets and checks even at night.
An enforcement team member checked the motorcycle's license plate.
I hear they'll add more enforcement teams in summer.

explain: 불법 주차, 쓰레기 무단 투기, 위생 같은 것을 확인하고 막는 팀이에요. '구청 단속반'처럼 앞에 기관 이름을 붙이는 경우가 많아요. 동사 '단속하다'와 같이 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The district office enforcement team checked parking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 기관 이름을 붙여서 어느 곳의 팀인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An institution name is put in front to say whose team it is.

phrases.en: They say the enforcement team comes out in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단속하러 현장에 온다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to mean the team comes to the scene to enforce rules.

phrases.en: The police crack down on illegal parking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단속반'이 하는 일을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for what an enforcement team does.

explain_en: It is a team that checks for and stops things like illegal parking, illegal dumping and hygiene violations. It is often preceded by an organization name, as in '구청 단속반'. It helps to learn it together with the verb '단속하다'.

examples.ko: 연화는 거절을 못 하고 그의 승용차에 동승했어요.
examples.en: Yeonhwa couldn't refuse and ended up riding in his car.

examples.ko: 택시에 친구와 동승해서 요금을 나눠 냈어요.
examples.en: I shared a taxi with a friend and split the fare.

examples.ko: 아이가 동승한 차는 더 천천히 운전해요.
examples.en: I drive more slowly when a child is riding in the car.
If we're going the same way, would you like to ride with me?

examples.ko: 친구가 동승해서 가는 길이 심심하지 않았어요.
examples.en: A friend rode along, so the trip wasn't boring.

examples.ko: 사고 때 차에 동승하지 않아서 다치지 않았어요.
examples.en: I wasn't in the car during the accident, so I wasn't hurt.

explain: 자동차, 택시, 배, 비행기처럼 같은 탈것에 함께 타는 것을 말해요. '~와/과 동승하다', '~에 동승하다'로 쓰고, 일상에서는 '같이 타다'라고 해요. 같이 탄 사람은 '동승자'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: Passengers must wear seat belts too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 차에 함께 탄 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person riding in the same vehicle.

phrases.en: If we're going the same way, may I ride with you?
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 같이 타도 되는지 정중하게 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask whether you may ride together.

phrases.en: Let's ride together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동승하다'를 일상 대화에서 말하는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday way to say '동승하다'.

explain_en: It means riding together in the same vehicle, such as a car, taxi, ship or plane. It is used as '~와/과 동승하다' or '~에 동승하다', and in daily talk people say '같이 타다'. A fellow passenger is a '동승자'.

examples.ko: 인터넷에 유명 배우를 봤다는 목격담이 올라왔어요.
examples.en: Sightings of a famous actor were posted online.

examples.ko: 경찰은 주민들의 목격담을 토대로 수사를 했어요.
examples.en: The police investigated based on the residents' eyewitness accounts.
Eyewitness accounts differ a little from person to person.

examples.ko: 저도 그날 본 것을 목격담으로 남겨 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll also leave what I saw that day as an eyewitness account.
Let me tell you one amazing eyewitness story.
According to eyewitness accounts, the fire started at dawn.

explain: 직접 본 사람이 들려주는 이야기를 말해요. 본 사람은 '목격자'라고 하고, 뉴스나 SNS에서는 '목격담이 올라오다/이어지다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사고를 봤다는 목격담이 계속 이어졌어요.
phrases.en: Eyewitness accounts of the accident kept coming in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 본 이야기를 계속 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many people keep sharing what they saw.

phrases.en: The witness told the police what they saw.
phrases.nuance_ko: '목격담'은 이야기이고, '목격자'는 직접 본 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 목격담 is the story; 목격자 is the person who saw it.

phrases.en: I left an account of what I saw of the accident in a comment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본 것을 글로 남길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when writing down what one saw.

explain_en: It is the story told by someone who saw something firsthand; the person who saw it is a '목격자'. In news and social media you often see '목격담이 올라오다/이어지다'.

en: to take care; to be cautious of one's health

examples.ko: 비가 오니까 감기 안 걸리게 몸조심하세요.
examples.en: It's raining, so take care not to catch a cold.
The weather is cold, so I have to look after my health.
After surgery, it's important to take care of yourself.
Take care on your trip and come back healthy.
My grandmother always tells me to take care of myself.
The exam is next week, so I'll take care of my health.

explain: '조심하세요'가 사고나 위험 앞에서 쓰는 말이라면 '몸조심하세요'는 감기, 피로, 부상 같은 건강 문제까지 걱정하는 인사예요. 아픈 사람이나 먼 길을 떠나는 사람에게 헤어질 때 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Take care so you don't catch a cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게 헤어질 때 하는 존댓말 인사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite goodbye used with elders or people you don't know well.

phrases.en: When we part, I tell my friend, 'Take care.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for friends and family.

phrases.en: You're going far, so take care and have a good trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멀리 떠나는 사람에게 건네는 말로 '-고'로 뒤 행동과 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said to someone leaving on a trip, linking to the next action with -고.
phrases.en_equiv: take care and come back safely

explain_en: '조심하세요' warns about accidents or danger, while '몸조심하세요' also worries about health problems like colds, fatigue and injuries. It is a common goodbye to someone who is sick or going on a long trip.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 매주 토요일 밤에 방영해요.
examples.en: This drama airs every Saturday night.

examples.ko: 방송국에서 새 예능 프로그램을 방영할 거예요.
examples.en: The broadcaster will air a new variety show.
The documentary that aired yesterday became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 그 방송사는 올림픽 경기를 생중계로 방영했어요.
examples.en: That network aired the Olympic games live.

examples.ko: 이 만화는 아이들이 보는 시간에 방영하고 있어요.
examples.en: This cartoon is airing at a time when kids watch.

examples.ko: 방영하는 동안 시청자들이 댓글을 많이 남겼어요.
examples.en: Viewers left lots of comments while it was airing.

explain: 드라마, 애니메이션, 다큐멘터리처럼 영상 프로그램을 내보낼 때 써요. 뉴스나 라디오에는 '방송하다'를 더 많이 써요. 지금 하고 있으면 '방영 중', 끝났으면 '방영이 끝났다'고 해요.

phrases.en: This drama will air starting tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 프로그램이 주어일 때 쓰는 피동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, with the program as the subject.

phrases.en: That drama is on air right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하고 있는 프로그램에 쓰는 짧은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase for a program currently airing.

phrases.en: They broadcast the news at nine in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 라디오까지 두루 쓰는 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that also covers news and radio.

explain_en: Use it for video programs such as dramas, animation, and documentaries. For news or radio, 방송하다 is more common. You say '방영 중' for something currently airing and '방영이 끝났다' once it has ended.

dis.h: air a TV program or drama
gh: broadcast on TV or radio, any content

p.n: 방송하다 is the general word; 방영하다 stresses airing the program itself.

t90.ax: This drama airs every Saturday night.

examples.en: The employees are grumbling that the pay is low.
When I sent my younger sibling on an errand, he answered in a sulky tone.

examples.ko: 갑자기 일정이 바뀌어서 여기저기서 볼멘소리가 나와요.
examples.en: The schedule suddenly changed, so grumbling is coming from all over.
Stop grumbling and get started on the work.

examples.ko: 아이가 볼멘소리로 '나만 못 가요?' 하고 물었어요.
examples.en: The child asked in a sulky voice, 'Am I the only one who can't go?'

examples.ko: 사장님은 직원들의 볼멘소리를 못 들은 척했어요.
examples.en: The boss pretended not to hear the employees' grumbling.

explain: 불만이 있어서 퉁명스럽고 투덜거리는 말투를 말해요. 보통 '볼멘소리를 하다', '볼멘소리가 나오다'로 써요. 그냥 '불평'은 내용이고, '볼멘소리'는 말투와 소리의 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: The child grumbles when told to do homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이고 불만스럽게 투덜거릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, used when someone grumbles in annoyance.

phrases.example: 일이 너무 많아서 여기저기서 볼멘소리가 나와요.
phrases.en: There is so much work that grumbling is coming from all around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람이 아니라 여러 사람의 불만이 들릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can also describe complaints heard from many people.

phrases.en: He answered in a sulky voice and left the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말의 내용보다 퉁명스러운 말투를 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It stresses the sullen tone rather than the content.

explain_en: It describes a curt, grumbling way of talking when someone is unhappy. It is usually used as '볼멘소리를 하다' or '볼멘소리가 나오다'. '불평' (complaint) focuses on the content, while '볼멘소리' focuses on the sulky tone.

examples.en: The singer started a nationwide tour.
I heard the tour tickets are already sold out.

examples.ko: 극단은 일 년 내내 순회공연을 다녀요.
examples.en: The theater troupe goes on tour all year round.
On this tour, they are coming to our city too.
The singer came back to Korea after finishing the tour.

examples.ko: 우리 학교에도 순회공연을 하러 오면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope they come to our school to perform on their tour.

explain: 여러 지역을 돌며 하는 공연이에요. 요즘 가수 이야기에서는 '투어'나 '전국 투어'라는 말도 많이 써요. '순회공연을 하다/다니다/마치다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 가수가 다음 달부터 전국 투어를 시작해요.
phrases.en: The singer starts a nationwide tour next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 가수나 팬들은 '순회공연' 대신 '투어'라는 말을 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Singers and fans today often say 투어 instead of 순회공연.

phrases.example: 극단이 두 달 동안의 순회공연을 마쳤어요.
phrases.en: The theater company finished its two-month tour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연 일정이 모두 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when all the performances on the schedule are over.

phrases.example: 그 밴드는 여름마다 여러 도시로 순회공연을 다녀요.
phrases.en: That band goes on tour to several cities every summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 지역을 계속 돌며 공연하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes going around to many regions and performing.

explain_en: It is a performance given while traveling through several regions. In talk about singers, people also say '투어' or '전국 투어'. It is used as '순회공연을 하다/다니다/마치다'.

examples.en: I bought acetone to remove my nail polish.

examples.ko: 아세톤 냄새가 너무 강해서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: The acetone smell was so strong that I opened the window.
I put acetone on cotton and wiped my nails.
Acetone burns easily, so be careful.

examples.ko: 아세톤이 피부에 닿으면 건조해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If acetone touches your skin, it can get dry.

examples.ko: 네일 가게에서 아세톤으로 젤 네일을 지웠어요.
examples.en: At the nail shop they removed my gel nails with acetone.

explain: 일상에서는 매니큐어를 지울 때 쓰는 액체로 가장 많이 만나요. 가게나 화장품 코너에서는 '네일 리무버'라고도 해요. 냄새가 강하고 불이 붙기 쉬워서 '조심하다'와 함께 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I removed the nail polish from my nails with acetone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매니큐어를 지울 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for removing nail polish.

phrases.en: I bought a nail polish remover at the store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장품 가게에서는 '아세톤'보다 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: At cosmetics stores, this is used more often than 아세톤.

phrases.en: Be careful when using acetone near fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 붙기 쉬워서 안전을 말할 때 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common safety phrase because it catches fire easily.

explain_en: In daily life you meet it mostly as the liquid used to remove nail polish. In shops and cosmetics aisles it is also called '네일 리무버'. It smells strong and burns easily, so it often comes with '조심하다'.

examples.ko: 감기약을 먹었는데 약발이 안 받는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I took cold medicine, but it doesn't seem to be working.

examples.ko: 약발은 보통 먹고 삼십 분쯤 지나야 나타나요.
examples.en: The medicine usually kicks in about thirty minutes after you take it.

examples.ko: 약발을 믿고 무리하면 더 아파질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you overdo it trusting the medicine's effect, you could get worse.

examples.ko: 약발도 오래가지 않아서 하루에 두 번 먹어요.
examples.en: The effect doesn't last long either, so I take it twice a day.

examples.ko: 진통제 약발 떨어지기 전에 다음 약을 챙겨요.
examples.en: I take the next dose before the painkiller wears off.

examples.ko: 약발이 센 약이라 먹으면 졸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a strong medicine, so it can make you sleepy.

explain: 약의 효과를 편하게 말하는 구어예요. '약발이 받다/안 받다', '약발이 떨어지다', '약발이 세다'처럼 자주 써요. 병원이나 설명서에서는 '효과'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This medicine works well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약이 효과가 있을 때 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say medicine is effective.

phrases.en: The medicine seems to have worn off, and my head hurts again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약 효과가 사라졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the effect of the medicine fades.

phrases.en: This cold medicine is strong, so it makes me sleepy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약 효과가 강하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the medicine's effect is strong.

explain_en: It is a casual spoken word for a medicine's effect. It is common in '약발이 받다/안 받다' (it works/doesn't work), '약발이 떨어지다' (it wears off) and '약발이 세다' (it's strong). In hospitals and on instructions people say '효과' instead.

examples.en: It rained a lot last evening.
I've had a headache since last evening.
Did you watch the news last evening?
I watched a movie with a friend last evening.
The food I ate last evening was really good.
I was tired last evening, so I fell asleep early.

explain: '어제저녁'을 줄인 말이라 어제 저녁만 가리켜요. 비슷하게 생긴 '엊그제'(그저께나 며칠 전)와 헷갈리지 마세요. 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I met a friend yesterday evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엊저녁'의 원래 말로, 글이나 말에서 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of '엊저녁', used in both writing and speech.

phrases.en: I got home late last evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간을 더 자세히 말할 때 뒤에 '늦게'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '늦게' to give a more specific time.

phrases.en: The food I ate last evening was delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-은' 형태의 꾸미는 말과 함께 쓰는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together with a '-은' modifier clause.

explain_en: It is a shortened form of '어제저녁', so it refers only to yesterday evening. Don't confuse it with the similar-looking '엊그제' (the day before yesterday or a few days ago). It has a casual, spoken feel.

t90.ax: It rained a lot last evening.

examples.en: He mumbled something under his breath.

examples.ko: 졸린 목소리로 웅얼웅얼 대답해서 잘 안 들렸어요.
examples.en: He answered in a sleepy mumble, so I couldn't hear well.
She muttered to herself and then fell asleep.

examples.ko: 웅얼웅얼 말하지 말고 크게 얘기해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't mumble, please speak up.
Grandfather murmured a prayer.

examples.ko: 마이크가 꺼진 줄 모르고 웅얼웅얼 불평했어요.
examples.en: Not knowing the mic was off, he grumbled in a mutter.

explain: 입속에서 소리가 흐려져서 말이 또렷하게 안 들리는 모습이에요. '중얼중얼'은 작은 소리로 혼자 계속 말하는 느낌이 강하고, 웅얼웅얼은 발음이 뭉개지는 느낌이 더 있어요. 말을 흐리는 사람에게 '웅얼거리지 마세요'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: He mumbled quietly, so I couldn't hear well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웅얼웅얼'을 동사로 바꾼 말로 말을 흐리는 행동을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '웅얼웅얼', meaning to mumble.

phrases.example: 웅얼웅얼 말하지 말고 크게 말해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please don't mumble; speak up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이 또렷하지 않게 들릴 때 '말하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '말하다' when speech sounds unclear.

phrases.en: He muttered numbers to himself to memorize them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 소리로 혼자 계속 말하는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense of quietly talking to oneself continuously.

explain_en: It describes speech that blurs inside the mouth so the words are unclear. '중얼중얼' leans toward quietly talking to oneself on and on, while 웅얼웅얼 has more of a slurred, unclear feel. You might also tell a mumbler '웅얼거리지 마세요'.
